custom_exercises.name: Scapular pull-up
custom_exercises.notes: Keep arms straight — this is a shoulder blade movement only, not a bend of the elbows.
custom_exercises.instructions: Hang from bar with arms fully extended. Depress and retract shoulder blades without bending elbows — body rises 2–3cm. Lower back to full hang. Repeat.

custom_exercises.name: Pull-up negative
custom_exercises.notes: Control the descent for a full 5–8 seconds — the eccentric is where the strength gains happen.
custom_exercises.instructions: Jump or step to the top position (chin over bar). Slowly lower yourself over 5–8 seconds with full control. Drop, reset, repeat.

custom_exercises.name: False grip dead hang
custom_exercises.notes: The wrist crease must sit on top of the ring — if it slips, the muscle-up transition becomes impossible.
custom_exercises.instructions: Place wrist crease over the top of each ring, fingers wrapping underneath. Hang with full body weight in false grip. Hold for target duration without letting grip slip.

custom_exercises.name: False grip ring row
custom_exercises.notes: Maintain false grip throughout the full range — it will feel like it wants to slip at the top; resist that.
custom_exercises.instructions: Set rings at chest height, adopt false grip, hang under rings at an angle. Pull chest to rings keeping wrists in false grip position. Lower with control.

custom_exercises.name: Ring dip negative
custom_exercises.notes: Keep rings turned out at the top and control the wobble — the instability is the point.
custom_exercises.instructions: Start in ring support hold (arms locked, rings turned out). Slowly lower into bottom of dip over 4–6 seconds. Step down or jump back to top and repeat.

custom_exercises.name: Back-to-wall handstand hold
custom_exercises.notes: Back-to-wall forces honest alignment — hollow body, no banana arch, and you learn where the real balance point lives.
custom_exercises.instructions: Walk feet up wall until body is vertical, back facing wall, heels lightly touching. Engage hollow body (ribs down, glutes on). Hold, then practice pulling one heel off the wall at a time.

custom_exercises.name: Shrimp squat
custom_exercises.notes: Keep the rear knee hovering just off the floor at the bottom — don't let it crash down.
custom_exercises.instructions: Stand on one leg, hold rear foot behind you with same-side hand. Squat down until rear knee nearly touches floor. Drive through front foot to stand. Progress by lowering rear knee closer to floor.

custom_exercises.name: One-leg L-sit
custom_exercises.notes: The extended leg must be fully locked and horizontal — a bent or drooping leg is a tuck sit, not a one-leg L-sit.
custom_exercises.instructions: From tuck sit on parallettes, extend one leg forward to horizontal, keeping the other tucked. Hold. Alternate legs. Progress to both legs extended.

custom_exercises.name: Single-leg box squat
custom_exercises.notes: Start with a high box and lower it over weeks — this is pure progressive overload for the pistol pattern.
custom_exercises.instructions: Stand on one leg in front of a box. Extend free leg forward, squat down to sit lightly on box. Pause, then drive up through heel to stand. Reduce box height as strength increases.

custom_exercises.name: Copenhagen plank
custom_exercises.notes: The top leg drives up into the bench — this is adductor loading, not just a side plank.
custom_exercises.instructions: Side plank position with top foot resting on a bench. Drive top leg up into the bench actively while holding plank alignment. Bottom leg can float or touch floor depending on level.

custom_exercises.name: Assisted pistol squat
custom_exercises.notes: Use the counterbalance to learn the movement pattern, not to avoid the hard part — gradually reduce assistance.
custom_exercises.instructions: Hold a pole, TRX, or extend arms forward holding a light weight as counterbalance. Lower into pistol squat with free leg extended. Stand using minimal assistance. Reduce support progressively.

custom_exercises.name: Pistol squat
custom_exercises.notes: Free leg stays extended and off the floor throughout — if it touches, it's a different exercise.
custom_exercises.instructions: Stand on one leg, extend free leg forward parallel to floor. Squat all the way down (hip crease below knee) keeping heel grounded. Drive through heel to stand fully. Keep torso upright.

custom_exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
custom_exercises.notes: Avoid swinging — initiate from the hip flexors with a slight posterior tilt, not from momentum.
custom_exercises.instructions: Dead hang from bar. Engage core and raise knees toward chest without swinging. Lower with control. Progress to one leg extended, then both legs.

custom_exercises.name: Tuck back lever hold
custom_exercises.notes: Hips must be at ring height — if they drop below, you've lost the lever position and are just hanging.
custom_exercises.instructions: From skin the cat, hold the inverted position. Tuck knees to chest and rotate until body is parallel to ground, face down. Hold with hips at ring level. Progression: tuck → advanced tuck → straddle → full.

custom_exercises.name: Tuck front lever hold
custom_exercises.notes: Pull the rings toward your hips actively — passive hanging will never build the front lever.
custom_exercises.instructions: From inverted hang, tuck knees to chest and lower body until parallel to ground, face up. Actively pull rings down toward hips. Hold. Progression: tuck → advanced tuck → straddle → full.
